questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A Direct Connect dedicated connection has been ordered and the colocation provider is ready to patch the circuit. What must be supplied to complete the physical handoff?

answers.text: Provide the LOA-CFA and confirm the port location, cross-connect details, optics, and speed settings
Use a single hosted zone for both internet and split-horizon private records without separation
Disable VPC route propagation and manage every prefix manually at scale
Use ALB access logs as the primary source for VPC-internal east-west traffic analysis

explanations.a: The facility can complete the cross-connect only when the authorization, port assignment, and physical interface details align.
explanations.b: Split-horizon DNS requires distinct public and private hosted zones for the same domain.
explanations.c: Manual route management does not scale; propagation from VGW/TGW is required for hybrid networks.
explanations.d: ALB logs only show traffic that reached the load balancer; VPC Flow Logs are the right tool for east-west analysis.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A company wants two 10 Gbps Direct Connect connections to behave as a single logical bundle. What should the engineer create?

answers.text: Treat AWS PrivateLink as a layer 3 routed mesh between VPCs
A Direct Connect link aggregation group using compatible dedicated connections
Use AWS Firewall Manager only after each account opts in individually with no central policy
Use ACM-imported certificates without renewal monitoring or alerting

explanations.a: PrivateLink is a unidirectional service-endpoint model, not a routed IP mesh.
explanations.b: A link aggregation group combines supported Direct Connect circuits for a single logical bundle with greater aggregate capacity.
explanations.c: Firewall Manager is designed for centralized policy at the org/OU level; per-account opt-in defeats the purpose.
explanations.d: Imported certificates do not auto-renew; expiry causes outages without monitoring.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A private virtual interface remains down after the circuit comes up. Which settings should be matched on the customer router?

answers.text: Place the customer gateway IP inside the VPC CIDR range
Choose subnets without ENA-supported instance types for high packet-per-second workloads
VLAN tag, BGP peer addresses, ASN, authentication if used, and allowed prefixes
Create a public hosted zone to serve only VPC-internal DNS queries

explanations.a: The customer gateway must be a public or routable IP outside the VPC CIDR; overlap breaks tunnel routing.
explanations.b: High-PPS workloads require ENA-supported instance types; non-ENA instances cap throughput.
explanations.c: A VIF requires the logical VLAN and BGP parameters to match before route exchange can occur.
explanations.d: Public hosted zones are authoritative on the internet; private VPC-only resolution requires a private hosted zone.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A hosted connection appears in the customer account but cannot be used yet. What is the required AWS-side step?

answers.text: Use AS_PATH prepending to make a path more preferred than its peer
Use Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints inside an isolated subnet without on-prem reachability
Use DNS TTL values as a hybrid routing protocol
Accept the hosted connection and create the required virtual interface

explanations.a: Prepending lengthens AS_PATH and makes a path less preferred, not more preferred.
explanations.b: Outbound endpoints need network reachability to on-prem resolvers via DX/VPN; isolation defeats the integration.
explanations.c: TTL controls how long a record is cached; it has no effect on packet routing decisions.
explanations.d: Hosted connectivity is not usable by the customer account until it is accepted and a VIF is configured.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A replication workload will use jumbo frames over Direct Connect. What must be validated before production traffic is moved?

answers.text: End-to-end MTU compatibility across routers, VIFs, AWS paths, and instances
Skip BFD and rely on default BGP keepalive timers for sub-second failover
Use a single shared CDK app deployed manually for production and dev
Advertise the same prefix from every BGP peer with identical attributes

explanations.a: Large frames work only when every segment in the data path supports the selected MTU.
explanations.b: Default BGP timers detect failure in tens of seconds; BFD is required for sub-second detection.
explanations.c: Dev and prod should be separate stacks/accounts with isolated state and pipelines.
explanations.d: Identical advertisements give the router no signal to choose between them; you need MED, AS_PATH, or LP differentiation.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: The AWS Direct Connect port is available, but the customer router does not show link up. What should be checked first?

answers.text: Use an external CA without ACM Private CA for AWS-native certificate distribution
Cross-connect status, optics, cabling, speed, duplex, and interface state
Use a Site-to-Site VPN as the only path for sustained 10 Gbps throughput
Use AWS PrivateLink to share full IP-level connectivity between two VPCs

explanations.a: AWS services integrate natively with ACM; an external CA without ACM PCA loses automated provisioning.
explanations.b: A physical link failure is most likely corrected by verifying the facility patch, transceivers, and interface negotiation.
explanations.c: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels are limited to ~1.25 Gbps each and are not the right design for sustained 10 Gbps; Direct Connect is.
explanations.d: PrivateLink exposes specific service endpoints, not full IP-level reachability; use peering or TGW for that.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A design requires resilience to a colocation facility failure. What implementation meets the requirement?

answers.text: Use the AWS CLI from a developer laptop as the production deployment automation tool
Use an ALB host-based routing rule to load balance non-HTTP TCP services
Provision redundant Direct Connect connections in separate locations with diverse customer equipment where possible
Use Global Accelerator to reduce data egress charges to on-premises

explanations.a: Production deployments need a controlled pipeline (CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, etc.) with auditability and least privilege.
explanations.b: ALB is HTTP/HTTPS only; non-HTTP TCP requires a Network Load Balancer.
explanations.c: Facility and equipment diversity reduces the chance that one site or router failure removes all private connectivity.
explanations.d: Global Accelerator improves anycast latency but does not reduce egress pricing to on-premises.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A dynamic Site-to-Site VPN tunnel is up, but no routes appear in the route table. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Use NLB cross-zone load balancing without enabling it explicitly per target group
Use CloudFront access logs to monitor inter-VPC traffic between private subnets
Use IP target groups for in-VPC EC2 targets that already have an instance ID
BGP ASN, tunnel inside addresses, peer configuration, and advertised prefixes

explanations.a: NLB cross-zone is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per target group.
explanations.b: CloudFront logs cover edge requests; VPC-internal east-west traffic is captured by VPC Flow Logs.
explanations.c: Instance target groups are simpler and follow Auto Scaling lifecycle; IP targets are for non-EC2 or cross-VPC IPs.
explanations.d: A working IPsec tunnel still needs correct BGP parameters and route advertisements before prefixes are learned.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Traffic should prefer Direct Connect and use VPN only during failure. What should be configured?

answers.text: BGP attributes and route preferences that make Direct Connect primary and VPN backup
Disable VPC Flow Logs and rely on application logs alone for network forensics
Use 169.254.x.x link-local addresses for production application traffic
Disable AWS Config to reduce read-API throttling on networking resources

explanations.a: Route attributes and advertisements control which hybrid path is preferred while preserving failover.
explanations.b: Application logs cannot reconstruct dropped packets, port scans, or layer 3/4 anomalies that flow logs capture.
explanations.c: Link-local addresses are reserved for tunnel endpoints (e.g., VPN BGP) and not valid for production data flows.
explanations.d: Config is needed for compliance and drift; disabling it does not address API throttling.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A static VPN route to a newly added on-premises CIDR is missing. What action is required?

answers.text: Use sticky sessions to compensate for missing identity tokens in API calls
Add the new CIDR to the VPN static routes and update corresponding on-premises routing
Skip CloudFormation drift detection and trust manual change tickets
Use a Direct Connect public VIF to reach a private VPC subnet

explanations.a: Stickiness binds a client to a target but does not authenticate or authorize requests.
explanations.b: Static routing does not learn new prefixes automatically, so each side must include the new destination.
explanations.c: Drift detection catches out-of-band changes that tickets often miss; it should run on a schedule.
explanations.d: Public VIFs reach AWS public service endpoints, not private VPC IP space; that requires a private or transit VIF.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A customer gateway has the wrong BGP ASN. What failure is most likely?

answers.text: Use IAM roles in place of resource policies for cross-account access
Use IAM policies to enforce VPC-to-VPC routing restrictions
The tunnel can establish IPsec while BGP route exchange fails
Use Reachability Analyzer for live packet capture and DPI

explanations.a: Cross-account access typically requires both: a trust policy on the role and a resource policy granting access.
explanations.b: IAM controls API authorization, not packet routing; routing decisions live in route tables and TGW route tables.
explanations.c: BGP neighbor identity and ASN settings must match the configured peers before routes are exchanged.
explanations.d: Reachability Analyzer is a static configuration analyzer; it does not perform live packet capture.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A more specific on-premises route is advertised over VPN than over Direct Connect. Why does traffic use VPN?

answers.text: Use a Route 53 alias record pointing to an on-premises IP
Use a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint to forward queries from VPCs to on-prem resolvers
Use a single route table for all subnets in a multi-tier VPC
Longest prefix match chooses the more specific VPN advertisement

explanations.a: Alias records target AWS resources by name; on-premises IPs require A/AAAA records or CNAMEs.
explanations.b: Inbound endpoints accept queries from on-prem; outbound endpoints forward VPC queries on-prem.
explanations.c: Public and private tiers need distinct route tables (e.g., IGW vs NAT) to enforce egress paths properly.
explanations.d: Prefix length can take precedence over other path preferences when one route is more specific.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A production attachment should not learn development routes through Transit Gateway. What should be configured?

answers.text: Separate Transit Gateway route table associations and propagations
Use BGP local preference on routes received from a remote AS to influence the remote AS choice
Use conditional forwarding rules instead of public hosted zones for internet-facing names
Change only an IAM password policy to fix a routing issue

explanations.a: Transit Gateway route table scope controls which attachments learn which prefixes.
explanations.b: Local preference is non-transitive and only affects outbound choice within the local AS; remote AS uses MED.
explanations.c: Conditional forwarders route DNS queries to specific resolvers; they do not publish authoritative public records.
explanations.d: IAM password policy governs human credentials; routing problems require route tables, BGP, or security group changes.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A branch prefix should be sent to AWS but not to other branches. Where should the filter be applied?

answers.text: Use Network ACLs as a stateful application-layer firewall
On the customer routing policy for the relevant BGP neighbors
Use a NAT gateway as a stateful inspection firewall for east-west traffic
Disable BGP MD5 authentication on a Direct Connect peering session

explanations.a: Network ACLs are stateless and operate at layers 3/4; they do not understand application protocols.
explanations.b: Route policy on the customer routers determines which prefixes are advertised to each peer.
explanations.c: NAT gateways translate addresses and do not inspect or filter east-west VPC traffic.
explanations.d: Disabling MD5 weakens the BGP session against spoofing and offers no operational benefit.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An on-premises firewall will terminate a Site-to-Site VPN to AWS. Which AWS object represents that device?

answers.text: Use CloudTrail to detect packet-level anomalies in VPC traffic
Use single-AZ deployments to reduce inter-AZ data transfer fees and improve resiliency
A customer gateway configured with the firewall public IP address and routing type
Manually document the setting in a spreadsheet only

explanations.a: CloudTrail records control-plane API calls; packet-level analysis requires VPC Flow Logs or Traffic Mirroring.
explanations.b: Single-AZ saves traffic costs but eliminates HA; resiliency requires multi-AZ.
explanations.c: The customer gateway defines the external peer that AWS uses to build the VPN connection.
explanations.d: Documentation alone does not enforce configuration; the change must exist in the AWS resources themselves.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A private VIF should provide access to many VPCs across Regions through a transit gateway. Which component is required?

answers.text: Use AWS Backup as a network configuration drift detection tool
Use VPC peering to lower data transfer cost between two Regions
Use hardcoded VPC IDs and subnet IDs in CloudFormation templates promoted across environments
A Direct Connect gateway associated with the transit gateway

explanations.a: AWS Backup is a data protection service and does not analyze network resource configuration.
explanations.b: Inter-Region peering still incurs cross-Region data transfer rates; the pricing is similar to other inter-Region paths.
explanations.c: Hardcoded resource IDs prevent reuse across environments; pass them as parameters or use cross-stack references.
explanations.d: A Direct Connect gateway enables a private or transit VIF to reach supported AWS gateway associations.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A provider-managed MPLS WAN will connect to AWS through Direct Connect. What must be coordinated with the provider?

answers.text: Circuit handoff, VLANs, BGP parameters, accepted prefixes, and failover behavior
Treat VPC Traffic Mirroring as a real-time alarm engine without a monitoring appliance
Use longer subnet masks on AWS than on-premises so on-prem always wins routing decisions
Connect SD-WAN appliances directly to a Direct Connect gateway without a Transit Gateway

explanations.a: Provider WAN integration succeeds when physical handoff and route exchange expectations are aligned.
explanations.b: Traffic Mirroring duplicates packets to a target appliance; alerts come from the appliance, not the mirror itself.
explanations.c: Longest-prefix match means the more specific route wins; this guarantees AWS wins, not on-prem.
explanations.d: SD-WAN integration uses Transit Gateway Connect (GRE+BGP); DXGW alone does not support SD-WAN attachments.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A VPN cannot establish because an on-premises firewall sits between peers. What should be allowed?

answers.text: Use NAT gateway in every private subnet to maximize redundancy and minimize latency
The IPsec negotiation and encapsulation traffic required by the AWS VPN tunnels
Use MX records to route HTTPS web traffic
Use a single Direct Connect connection without redundancy or VPN backup

explanations.a: One NAT gateway per AZ is the recommended pattern; per-subnet NAT inflates cost without resilience benefit.
explanations.b: The firewall must permit the protocols and ports used to build and carry the encrypted VPN tunnel.
explanations.c: MX records direct mail delivery; web traffic uses A/AAAA, alias, or CNAME records.
explanations.d: A single DX violates resilience guidance; AWS recommends two diverse circuits or a VPN backup.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Direct Connect must attach to a transit gateway. What VIF type should be used?

answers.text: Use overlapping CIDRs across all VPCs and let routing protocols resolve conflicts
Use a default route to the Internet Gateway in private subnets that need NAT
A transit virtual interface through a Direct Connect gateway
Use a transit VIF to reach a VPC without a Transit Gateway attachment

explanations.a: AWS networking does not arbitrate overlapping CIDRs; address conflicts must be designed out before connecting VPCs.
explanations.b: A default route to the IGW makes the subnet public; private subnets must point default to a NAT gateway.
explanations.c: Transit VIFs connect Direct Connect connectivity into transit gateways through Direct Connect gateways.
explanations.d: Transit VIFs terminate on a Direct Connect gateway connected to a Transit Gateway; without a TGW the VPC is unreachable.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises clients reach one VPC through Transit Gateway but not a second VPC. What should be checked?

answers.text: Use a Route 53 health check to register a domain name
Use full-mesh VPN tunnels to scale to hundreds of VPCs
Use AWS WAF as a layer 4 firewall for non-HTTP TCP traffic
Transit Gateway route table associations, propagations, VPC routes, and return paths

explanations.a: Domain registration is a separate Route 53 operation; health checks only monitor endpoints.
explanations.b: Full-mesh VPN scales as O(n^2) and quickly hits operational limits; Transit Gateway is the scalable hub.
explanations.c: WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS only; layer 4 protection comes from security groups, NACLs, or Network Firewall.
explanations.d: Both the hub route table and the spoke VPC route tables must contain the necessary forward and return routes.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A company changes a VPN from static routing to BGP. Which configuration must be updated?

answers.text: The customer gateway and VPN connection settings for dynamic routing
Use the same BGP ASN on both sides of an eBGP session over Direct Connect
Configure jumbo frames on a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Use AWS Config to capture per-packet flow data

explanations.a: Dynamic routing requires AWS and customer gateway settings that support BGP neighbors and advertisements.
explanations.b: eBGP requires different ASNs on each side; identical ASNs cause routes to be rejected as loops.
explanations.c: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames; MTU is fixed at 1500 with lower MSS after IPsec overhead.
explanations.d: Config tracks resource configuration changes, not network packet data.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises clients must resolve records in an AWS private hosted zone. What should be configured?

answers.text: Use an ACM public certificate to sign internal mTLS traffic between EC2 instances
Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints and on-premises conditional forwarders
Send VPC Flow Logs only to local instance memory for short-term review
Use VPC sharing to share security groups across non-shared subnets

explanations.a: Public ACM certs are issued for public domains; internal mTLS uses ACM Private CA.
explanations.b: Inbound endpoints let corporate DNS forward selected private AWS names to the VPC resolver path.
explanations.c: Flow logs must be delivered to S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Firehose; instance memory is not a supported destination.
explanations.d: Security group sharing follows shared subnets; non-shared subnets cannot reference cross-account security groups.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: AWS instances must resolve corp.example.com from on-premises DNS. What is required?

answers.text: Use Transit Gateway Connect over IPsec instead of GRE
Use a security group as the authoritative DNS zone
Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints with a forwarding rule for corp.example.com
Use Transit Gateway Network Manager as a real-time intrusion detection engine

explanations.a: Transit Gateway Connect uses GRE encapsulation with BGP; IPsec is not the supported transport for Connect attachments.
explanations.b: Security groups filter packets at ENIs; they have no DNS authority or zone-serving capability.
explanations.c: Outbound endpoints forward selected VPC resolver queries to on-premises DNS servers.
explanations.d: Network Manager provides topology and event monitoring; intrusion detection belongs to GuardDuty or third-party IDS.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A hybrid DNS rule uses one on-premises DNS server and resolution fails during maintenance. What should be improved?

answers.text: Use Transit Gateway to connect VPCs that share identical primary CIDR blocks without translation
Connect EC2 instances directly to a Direct Connect dedicated port without a VIF
Use VPC peering to provide transitive routing through a hub VPC
Add multiple reachable DNS targets and monitor resolver health

explanations.a: Transit Gateway requires non-overlapping CIDRs between attached VPCs unless NAT or PrivateLink mediates traffic.
explanations.b: Traffic on Direct Connect must traverse a VIF (private/public/transit); EC2 instances cannot peer with the port directly.
explanations.c: VPC peering is non-transitive; a hub VPC cannot relay traffic between two peered spokes.
explanations.d: Multiple DNS targets reduce dependency on a single on-premises resolver during maintenance or failure.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A private hosted zone is associated with a VPC, but corporate clients receive NXDOMAIN. What should be verified?

answers.text: The conditional forwarder suffix, inbound endpoint reachability, and hosted zone association
Use a NAT gateway as the application load balancer
Use AWS Cloud Map as a layer 4 transparent proxy
Use TLS passthrough on an ALB to inspect HTTPS payloads

explanations.a: The query must be forwarded to the correct endpoint, and that endpoint must have visibility to the private zone.
explanations.b: NAT gateways translate addresses for outbound traffic and have no listener, target group, or layer 7 capability.
explanations.c: Cloud Map is a service registry returning DNS or API answers; it does not proxy traffic.
explanations.d: ALB always terminates TLS at the listener; passthrough is a Network Load Balancer behavior.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Several VPCs in different accounts need the same private namespace. What should be done?

answers.text: Use AWS RAM to share an Internet Gateway across multiple accounts
Associate the private hosted zone with each required VPC or use supported sharing
Use service-linked roles as a substitute for security groups
Use a single Lambda function in place of an Application Load Balancer for path-based routing

explanations.a: Internet Gateways are not shareable resources in AWS RAM; each VPC has its own IGW.
explanations.b: Private DNS visibility follows VPC association, including cross-account association where configured.
explanations.c: Service-linked roles grant API permissions to AWS services; they do not gate network traffic.
explanations.d: A Lambda function as the front door does not provide listeners, sticky sessions, or load balancing semantics.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A resolver loop appears between AWS and on-premises DNS. What should be corrected?

answers.text: Configure DNSSEC by adding a TXT record only, without DS or KSK setup
Skip IaC and rely on point-in-time AWS Console screenshots for repeatability
Conditional forwarding boundaries so each suffix is sent only to its authoritative resolver
Use static routes only on a BGP-capable Direct Connect for change management

explanations.a: DNSSEC requires a Key Signing Key in Route 53 and a DS record published at the parent zone; a TXT record alone does nothing.
explanations.b: Screenshots cannot be replayed and do not capture dependencies; IaC is the supported path.
explanations.c: Clear authoritative ownership prevents the same query from being forwarded back and forth until timeout.
explanations.d: Direct Connect requires BGP for the peering session; static-only configuration is not supported on the AWS side.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises workloads should resolve AWS service names to interface endpoint private IPs. What must be enabled?

answers.text: Use an ALB listener rule for routing between networks
Use AWS Trusted Advisor as a packet-capture utility
Use a centralized egress VPC without route tables that point to the inspection appliance
Private DNS for the endpoint with forwarding to the VPC resolver path

explanations.a: ALB listener rules route HTTP requests to target groups; they do not route between VPCs or hybrid networks.
explanations.b: Trusted Advisor is a best-practice checker, not a packet-capture tool.
explanations.c: Centralized egress requires explicit route table entries pointing to the firewall/proxy in the inspection VPC.
explanations.d: Private DNS maps supported AWS service names to endpoint addresses within the associated VPC resolver context.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: AWS clients need private HTTP access to legacy on-premises servers over Direct Connect with path-based routing. What should be created?

answers.text: An internal Application Load Balancer with IP targets
Use only CloudFront cache settings to control private VPC routing
Use a Classic Load Balancer for new HTTP/2 and gRPC workloads
Use VPC peering to extend multicast across VPCs without Transit Gateway multicast support

explanations.a: An internal ALB can use reachable IP targets and layer 7 routing for private hybrid applications.
explanations.b: CloudFront cache controls edge caching, not VPC routing or hybrid traffic flow.
explanations.c: Classic Load Balancer does not support HTTP/2 or gRPC; ALB is required.
explanations.d: VPC peering does not propagate multicast; Transit Gateway multicast domains are required.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A TCP service in a data center needs stable private load-balanced access from VPC workloads. Which option fits?

answers.text: Use IGMP snooping at the security group level
A Network Load Balancer with IP targets
Use a private hosted zone associated with one VPC to resolve names from a peered VPC without re-association
Skip route summarization and advertise every /32 host route across the WAN

explanations.a: Security groups operate per ENI and do not implement IGMP snooping; that is a switch-fabric feature.
explanations.b: NLB supports layer 4 balancing to reachable IP targets, including supported hybrid targets.
explanations.c: Private hosted zones must be associated with each VPC that needs to resolve their records, even across peering.
explanations.d: Per-host routes inflate the routing table and exceed BGP limits on Direct Connect (typically 100 prefixes).

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Traffic must be transparently distributed to firewall appliances. What load balancing service is appropriate?

answers.text: Disable VPC route propagation and manage every prefix manually at scale
Use a single hosted zone for both internet and split-horizon private records without separation
Gateway Load Balancer with appliance target groups
Use service control policies in place of route table entries

explanations.a: Manual route management does not scale; propagation from VGW/TGW is required for hybrid networks.
explanations.b: Split-horizon DNS requires distinct public and private hosted zones for the same domain.
explanations.c: Gateway Load Balancer is designed for transparent appliance insertion with GENEVE encapsulation.
explanations.d: SCPs restrict API actions across accounts and have no effect on dataplane routing.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An ECS service uses dynamic host ports behind an ALB. What must be configured?

answers.text: Use ACM-imported certificates without renewal monitoring or alerting
Treat AWS PrivateLink as a layer 3 routed mesh between VPCs
Skip TLS in transit because IPsec already encrypts at layer 3
ECS service registration with the correct target group and target type

explanations.a: Imported certificates do not auto-renew; expiry causes outages without monitoring.
explanations.b: PrivateLink is a unidirectional service-endpoint model, not a routed IP mesh.
explanations.c: IPsec encryption ends at the tunnel termination; defense in depth still recommends TLS for application traffic.
explanations.d: The service must register current task endpoints so the ALB can route to the active containers.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Backends need the original client address for authorization decisions. What feature should be considered?

answers.text: Source IP preservation or Proxy Protocol v2, depending on load balancer and target type
Place the customer gateway IP inside the VPC CIDR range
Create a public hosted zone to serve only VPC-internal DNS queries
Use ALB access logs as the primary source for VPC-internal east-west traffic analysis

explanations.a: The backend can receive client source context through supported load balancer mechanisms.
explanations.b: The customer gateway must be a public or routable IP outside the VPC CIDR; overlap breaks tunnel routing.
explanations.c: Public hosted zones are authoritative on the internet; private VPC-only resolution requires a private hosted zone.
explanations.d: ALB logs only show traffic that reached the load balancer; VPC Flow Logs are the right tool for east-west analysis.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Users must authenticate with OIDC before the ALB forwards requests. What should be configured?

answers.text: Use DNS TTL values as a hybrid routing protocol
An ALB listener authentication action using the OIDC provider
Choose subnets without ENA-supported instance types for high packet-per-second workloads
Use AS_PATH prepending to make a path more preferred than its peer

explanations.a: TTL controls how long a record is cached; it has no effect on packet routing decisions.
explanations.b: ALB listener actions can authenticate users before forwarding HTTP requests to targets.
explanations.c: High-PPS workloads require ENA-supported instance types; non-ENA instances cap throughput.
explanations.d: Prepending lengthens AS_PATH and makes a path less preferred, not more preferred.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Targets pass TCP checks but fail real application requests. What should be updated?

answers.text: Use VPC interface endpoints to expose your services to the public internet
Advertise the same prefix from every BGP peer with identical attributes
Use a health check path or protocol that validates application readiness
Use AWS Firewall Manager only after each account opts in individually with no central policy

explanations.a: Interface endpoints provide private connectivity into AWS; public exposure uses ALB/NLB or PrivateLink-as-provider.
explanations.b: Identical advertisements give the router no signal to choose between them; you need MED, AS_PATH, or LP differentiation.
explanations.c: Health checks should represent whether a target can actually serve production traffic.
explanations.d: Firewall Manager is designed for centralized policy at the org/OU level; per-account opt-in defeats the purpose.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A new Transit Gateway must provide visibility into traffic by attachment. What should be enabled?

answers.text: Use an external CA without ACM Private CA for AWS-native certificate distribution
Use a single shared CDK app deployed manually for production and dev
Use a Site-to-Site VPN as the only path for sustained 10 Gbps throughput
Transit Gateway Flow Logs to a central destination

explanations.a: AWS services integrate natively with ACM; an external CA without ACM PCA loses automated provisioning.
explanations.b: Dev and prod should be separate stacks/accounts with isolated state and pipelines.
explanations.c: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels are limited to ~1.25 Gbps each and are not the right design for sustained 10 Gbps; Direct Connect is.
explanations.d: Transit Gateway Flow Logs capture metadata for traffic that crosses attachments.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Operations needs an alert when Direct Connect BGP drops. What should be configured?

answers.text: CloudWatch alarms for Direct Connect connection and BGP state metrics
Skip BFD and rely on default BGP keepalive timers for sub-second failover
Use Global Accelerator to reduce data egress charges to on-premises
Use the AWS CLI from a developer laptop as the production deployment automation tool

explanations.a: Direct Connect metrics can trigger alarms when link or routing state changes.
explanations.b: Default BGP timers detect failure in tens of seconds; BFD is required for sub-second detection.
explanations.c: Global Accelerator improves anycast latency but does not reduce egress pricing to on-premises.
explanations.d: Production deployments need a controlled pipeline (CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, etc.) with auditability and least privilege.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An internet-facing ALB requires request troubleshooting records. What should be enabled?

answers.text: Use Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints inside an isolated subnet without on-prem reachability
ALB access logs delivered to a protected S3 bucket
Use IP target groups for in-VPC EC2 targets that already have an instance ID
Use CloudFront access logs to monitor inter-VPC traffic between private subnets

explanations.a: Outbound endpoints need network reachability to on-prem resolvers via DX/VPN; isolation defeats the integration.
explanations.b: ALB access logs provide request-level evidence for troubleshooting and security analysis.
explanations.c: Instance target groups are simpler and follow Auto Scaling lifecycle; IP targets are for non-EC2 or cross-VPC IPs.
explanations.d: CloudFront logs cover edge requests; VPC-internal east-west traffic is captured by VPC Flow Logs.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A public API uses CloudFront and AWS WAF. The team needs rule matches and viewer context. Which logs are needed?

answers.text: Disable AWS Config to reduce read-API throttling on networking resources
Use an ALB host-based routing rule to load balance non-HTTP TCP services
AWS WAF logs plus CloudFront access or real-time logs
Use 169.254.x.x link-local addresses for production application traffic

explanations.a: Config is needed for compliance and drift; disabling it does not address API throttling.
explanations.b: ALB is HTTP/HTTPS only; non-HTTP TCP requires a Network Load Balancer.
explanations.c: WAF records rule decisions, while CloudFront records edge viewer request details.
explanations.d: Link-local addresses are reserved for tunnel endpoints (e.g., VPN BGP) and not valid for production data flows.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Packet payloads from a specific EC2 ENI must be captured for analysis. Which feature is appropriate?

answers.text: Use sticky sessions to compensate for missing identity tokens in API calls
Skip CloudFormation drift detection and trust manual change tickets
Use NLB cross-zone load balancing without enabling it explicitly per target group
VPC Traffic Mirroring with a filter and capture appliance

explanations.a: Stickiness binds a client to a target but does not authenticate or authorize requests.
explanations.b: Drift detection catches out-of-band changes that tickets often miss; it should run on a schedule.
explanations.c: NLB cross-zone is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per target group.
explanations.d: Traffic Mirroring copies selected packets to inspection tools for deeper analysis.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Centralized egress uses AWS Network Firewall. What should be logged?

answers.text: Network Firewall alert and flow logs with rule context
Use IAM roles in place of resource policies for cross-account access
Use Reachability Analyzer for live packet capture and DPI
Use a Direct Connect public VIF to reach a private VPC subnet

explanations.a: Firewall logs show which flows matched policies and whether traffic was allowed or rejected.
explanations.b: Cross-account access typically requires both: a trust policy on the role and a resource policy granting access.
explanations.c: Reachability Analyzer is a static configuration analyzer; it does not perform live packet capture.
explanations.d: Public VIFs reach AWS public service endpoints, not private VPC IP space; that requires a private or transit VIF.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Applications time out through an interface endpoint. What telemetry should be collected?

answers.text: Use a Route 53 alias record pointing to an on-premises IP
Endpoint metrics where available, VPC Flow Logs, service health events, and application errors
Use a single route table for all subnets in a multi-tier VPC
Use AWS PrivateLink to share full IP-level connectivity between two VPCs

explanations.a: Alias records target AWS resources by name; on-premises IPs require A/AAAA records or CNAMEs.
explanations.b: Endpoint troubleshooting needs network metadata and application symptoms from the same time window.
explanations.c: Public and private tiers need distinct route tables (e.g., IGW vs NAT) to enforce egress paths properly.
explanations.d: PrivateLink exposes specific service endpoints, not full IP-level reachability; use peering or TGW for that.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A team must prove that a VPC route to on-premises is permitted after Direct Connect implementation. Which tool can help?

answers.text: Change only an IAM password policy to fix a routing issue
Disable VPC Flow Logs and rely on application logs alone for network forensics
VPC Reachability Analyzer for the intended source and destination
Use IAM policies to enforce VPC-to-VPC routing restrictions

explanations.a: IAM password policy governs human credentials; routing problems require route tables, BGP, or security group changes.
explanations.b: Application logs cannot reconstruct dropped packets, port scans, or layer 3/4 anomalies that flow logs capture.
explanations.c: Reachability Analyzer evaluates whether AWS network configuration permits a defined path.
explanations.d: IAM controls API authorization, not packet routing; routing decisions live in route tables and TGW route tables.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A VPN tunnel is up, but application traffic fails. What should be tested?

answers.text: Use conditional forwarding rules instead of public hosted zones for internet-facing names
Use BGP local preference on routes received from a remote AS to influence the remote AS choice
Use a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint to forward queries from VPCs to on-prem resolvers
Forward path, return path, route tables, security groups, NACLs, and on-premises firewall rules

explanations.a: Conditional forwarders route DNS queries to specific resolvers; they do not publish authoritative public records.
explanations.b: Local preference is non-transitive and only affects outbound choice within the local AS; remote AS uses MED.
explanations.c: Inbound endpoints accept queries from on-prem; outbound endpoints forward VPC queries on-prem.
explanations.d: Tunnel state alone does not prove the full application data path is allowed in both directions.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Development and production attach to the same Transit Gateway. The design requires isolation. What validation is appropriate?

answers.text: Reachability tests for both allowed shared-service paths and denied development-to-production paths
Use a NAT gateway as a stateful inspection firewall for east-west traffic
Manually document the setting in a spreadsheet only
Use Network ACLs as a stateful application-layer firewall

explanations.a: A proper validation proves required connectivity works and prohibited reachability is blocked.
explanations.b: NAT gateways translate addresses and do not inspect or filter east-west VPC traffic.
explanations.c: Documentation alone does not enforce configuration; the change must exist in the AWS resources themselves.
explanations.d: Network ACLs are stateless and operate at layers 3/4; they do not understand application protocols.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Hybrid DNS is complete. What validates it?

answers.text: Use VPC peering to lower data transfer cost between two Regions
Resolve AWS private names from on-premises and on-premises names from AWS, then confirm query paths
Use hardcoded VPC IDs and subnet IDs in CloudFormation templates promoted across environments
Use AWS Backup as a network configuration drift detection tool

explanations.a: Inter-Region peering still incurs cross-Region data transfer rates; the pricing is similar to other inter-Region paths.
explanations.b: Both lookup directions must be tested through the intended Resolver endpoints and forwarding rules.
explanations.c: Hardcoded resource IDs prevent reuse across environments; pass them as parameters or use cross-stack references.
explanations.d: AWS Backup is a data protection service and does not analyze network resource configuration.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A firewall is inserted between VPCs before cutover. What should be validated?

answers.text: Connect SD-WAN appliances directly to a Direct Connect gateway without a Transit Gateway
Disable BGP MD5 authentication on a Direct Connect peering session
Representative allowed flows, expected blocked flows, asymmetric routing cases, and firewall logs
Use longer subnet masks on AWS than on-premises so on-prem always wins routing decisions

explanations.a: SD-WAN integration uses Transit Gateway Connect (GRE+BGP); DXGW alone does not support SD-WAN attachments.
explanations.b: Disabling MD5 weakens the BGP session against spoofing and offers no operational benefit.
explanations.c: Cutover testing must prove policy behavior and confirm that evidence appears in inspection logs.
explanations.d: Longest-prefix match means the more specific route wins; this guarantees AWS wins, not on-prem.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Traffic is migrated from VPN to Direct Connect. How should success be confirmed?

answers.text: Use NAT gateway in every private subnet to maximize redundancy and minimize latency
Use MX records to route HTTPS web traffic
Use CloudTrail to detect packet-level anomalies in VPC traffic
Check route preference, path traces, throughput, latency, and application success over Direct Connect

explanations.a: One NAT gateway per AZ is the recommended pattern; per-subnet NAT inflates cost without resilience benefit.
explanations.b: MX records direct mail delivery; web traffic uses A/AAAA, alias, or CNAME records.
explanations.c: CloudTrail records control-plane API calls; packet-level analysis requires VPC Flow Logs or Traffic Mirroring.
explanations.d: Migration validation should prove traffic uses the intended path and meets performance expectations.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A private database subnet cannot be reached from an application subnet in the same VPC.

answers.text: Configure route tables and security groups for the required private application-to-database flow
Use a default route to the Internet Gateway in private subnets that need NAT
Use single-AZ deployments to reduce inter-AZ data transfer fees and improve resiliency
Use a transit VIF to reach a VPC without a Transit Gateway attachment

explanations.a: VPC communication needs both a valid route path and security controls that allow the intended ports.
explanations.b: A default route to the IGW makes the subnet public; private subnets must point default to a NAT gateway.
explanations.c: Single-AZ saves traffic costs but eliminates HA; resiliency requires multi-AZ.
explanations.d: Transit VIFs terminate on a Direct Connect gateway connected to a Transit Gateway; without a TGW the VPC is unreachable.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Two non-overlapping VPCs need simple direct connectivity with no transit requirement.

answers.text: Use a Route 53 health check to register a domain name
Create a VPC peering connection and add reciprocal routes
Use AWS WAF as a layer 4 firewall for non-HTTP TCP traffic
Use full-mesh VPN tunnels to scale to hundreds of VPCs

explanations.a: Domain registration is a separate Route 53 operation; health checks only monitor endpoints.
explanations.b: Peering is appropriate for direct private connectivity between two non-overlapping VPCs.
explanations.c: WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS only; layer 4 protection comes from security groups, NACLs, or Network Firewall.
explanations.d: Full-mesh VPN scales as O(n^2) and quickly hits operational limits; Transit Gateway is the scalable hub.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Thirty VPCs need centralized routing.

answers.text: Configure jumbo frames on a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Use the same BGP ASN on both sides of an eBGP session over Direct Connect
Attach VPCs to Transit Gateway and configure route tables
Use a single Direct Connect connection without redundancy or VPN backup

explanations.a: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames; MTU is fixed at 1500 with lower MSS after IPsec overhead.
explanations.b: eBGP requires different ASNs on each side; identical ASNs cause routes to be rejected as loops.
explanations.c: Transit Gateway simplifies scalable multi-VPC routing and segmentation.
explanations.d: A single DX violates resilience guidance; AWS recommends two diverse circuits or a VPN backup.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A provider exposes one private service to many consumers.

answers.text: Use AWS Config to capture per-packet flow data
Use VPC sharing to share security groups across non-shared subnets
Use an ACM public certificate to sign internal mTLS traffic between EC2 instances
Create a PrivateLink endpoint service and consumer interface endpoints

explanations.a: Config tracks resource configuration changes, not network packet data.
explanations.b: Security group sharing follows shared subnets; non-shared subnets cannot reference cross-account security groups.
explanations.c: Public ACM certs are issued for public domains; internal mTLS uses ACM Private CA.
explanations.d: PrivateLink provides service-level connectivity without broad VPC route access.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A Transit Gateway spoke cannot reach shared services.

answers.text: Add the required Transit Gateway and VPC route table entries
Use Transit Gateway Network Manager as a real-time intrusion detection engine
Use a security group as the authoritative DNS zone
Send VPC Flow Logs only to local instance memory for short-term review

explanations.a: Both the spoke VPC and Transit Gateway route tables must contain the correct paths.
explanations.b: Network Manager provides topology and event monitoring; intrusion detection belongs to GuardDuty or third-party IDS.
explanations.c: Security groups filter packets at ENIs; they have no DNS authority or zone-serving capability.
explanations.d: Flow logs must be delivered to S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Firehose; instance memory is not a supported destination.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Instances receive the wrong DNS server in a VPC.

answers.text: Treat VPC Traffic Mirroring as a real-time alarm engine without a monitoring appliance
Update the VPC DHCP option set association and resolver settings
Use overlapping CIDRs across all VPCs and let routing protocols resolve conflicts
Use Transit Gateway Connect over IPsec instead of GRE

explanations.a: Traffic Mirroring duplicates packets to a target appliance; alerts come from the appliance, not the mirror itself.
explanations.b: DHCP options influence DNS server values that instances use after renewal or launch.
explanations.c: AWS networking does not arbitrate overlapping CIDRs; address conflicts must be designed out before connecting VPCs.
explanations.d: Transit Gateway Connect uses GRE encapsulation with BGP; IPsec is not the supported transport for Connect attachments.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An SD-WAN appliance supports GRE and BGP.

answers.text: Use VPC peering to provide transitive routing through a hub VPC
Connect EC2 instances directly to a Direct Connect dedicated port without a VIF
Create a Transit Gateway Connect attachment with GRE and BGP peers
Use TLS passthrough on an ALB to inspect HTTPS payloads

explanations.a: VPC peering is non-transitive; a hub VPC cannot relay traffic between two peered spokes.
explanations.b: Traffic on Direct Connect must traverse a VIF (private/public/transit); EC2 instances cannot peer with the port directly.
explanations.c: Transit Gateway Connect is built for GRE/BGP SD-WAN integration.
explanations.d: ALB always terminates TLS at the listener; passthrough is a Network Load Balancer behavior.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A third-party firewall fleet must inspect VPC traffic.

answers.text: Use a single Lambda function in place of an Application Load Balancer for path-based routing
Use Transit Gateway to connect VPCs that share identical primary CIDR blocks without translation
Use service-linked roles as a substitute for security groups
Use Gateway Load Balancer endpoints with route-table steering

explanations.a: A Lambda function as the front door does not provide listeners, sticky sessions, or load balancing semantics.
explanations.b: Transit Gateway requires non-overlapping CIDRs between attached VPCs unless NAT or PrivateLink mediates traffic.
explanations.c: Service-linked roles grant API permissions to AWS services; they do not gate network traffic.
explanations.d: GWLB endpoints and routes can insert appliances into traffic paths.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A provider MPLS WAN must exchange routes with AWS.

answers.text: Coordinate BGP prefixes, route filters, and failover behavior with the provider
Use static routes only on a BGP-capable Direct Connect for change management
Use AWS Cloud Map as a layer 4 transparent proxy
Configure DNSSEC by adding a TXT record only, without DS or KSK setup

explanations.a: Provider integration depends on matching route policy and operational expectations.
explanations.b: Direct Connect requires BGP for the peering session; static-only configuration is not supported on the AWS side.
explanations.c: Cloud Map is a service registry returning DNS or API answers; it does not proxy traffic.
explanations.d: DNSSEC requires a Key Signing Key in Route 53 and a DS record published at the parent zone; a TXT record alone does nothing.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A vendor advertises a default route that attracts all VPC egress.

answers.text: Use an ALB listener rule for routing between networks
Apply route filters and restrict Transit Gateway propagation
Use AWS Trusted Advisor as a packet-capture utility
Use AWS RAM to share an Internet Gateway across multiple accounts

explanations.a: ALB listener rules route HTTP requests to target groups; they do not route between VPCs or hybrid networks.
explanations.b: Filtering prevents unintended prefixes from spreading through the AWS network.
explanations.c: Trusted Advisor is a best-practice checker, not a packet-capture tool.
explanations.d: Internet Gateways are not shareable resources in AWS RAM; each VPC has its own IGW.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Branch VPN tunnels terminate on a vendor appliance in AWS.

answers.text: Use a Classic Load Balancer for new HTTP/2 and gRPC workloads
Use a NAT gateway as the application load balancer
Configure appliance ENIs, routes toward the appliance, and health-aware failover
Use a centralized egress VPC without route tables that point to the inspection appliance

explanations.a: Classic Load Balancer does not support HTTP/2 or gRPC; ALB is required.
explanations.b: NAT gateways translate addresses for outbound traffic and have no listener, target group, or layer 7 capability.
explanations.c: The AWS route tables must steer branch traffic to healthy appliance paths.
explanations.d: Centralized egress requires explicit route table entries pointing to the firewall/proxy in the inspection VPC.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A partner router only needs BGP exchange.

answers.text: Skip IaC and rely on point-in-time AWS Console screenshots for repeatability
Use a private hosted zone associated with one VPC to resolve names from a peered VPC without re-association
Use VPC peering to extend multicast across VPCs without Transit Gateway multicast support
Provide BGP parameters and prefix policy without AWS IAM credentials

explanations.a: Screenshots cannot be replayed and do not capture dependencies; IaC is the supported path.
explanations.b: Private hosted zones must be associated with each VPC that needs to resolve their records, even across peering.
explanations.c: VPC peering does not propagate multicast; Transit Gateway multicast domains are required.
explanations.d: BGP peering uses network configuration; cloud control-plane credentials are unnecessary.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Spokes must reach shared services but not other spokes.

answers.text: Use separate Transit Gateway route tables with controlled propagation
Use only CloudFront cache settings to control private VPC routing
Use a single hosted zone for both internet and split-horizon private records without separation
Disable VPC route propagation and manage every prefix manually at scale

explanations.a: Route table segmentation enforces the hub-and-spoke reachability model.
explanations.b: CloudFront cache controls edge caching, not VPC routing or hybrid traffic flow.
explanations.c: Split-horizon DNS requires distinct public and private hosted zones for the same domain.
explanations.d: Manual route management does not scale; propagation from VGW/TGW is required for hybrid networks.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A new spoke cannot reach central egress.

answers.text: Use IGMP snooping at the security group level
Add spoke subnet routes to Transit Gateway and hub routes to the egress attachment
Use service control policies in place of route table entries
Skip TLS in transit because IPsec already encrypts at layer 3

explanations.a: Security groups operate per ENI and do not implement IGMP snooping; that is a switch-fabric feature.
explanations.b: Both sides of the hub path need explicit routing.
explanations.c: SCPs restrict API actions across accounts and have no effect on dataplane routing.
explanations.d: IPsec encryption ends at the tunnel termination; defense in depth still recommends TLS for application traffic.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Spoke-to-spoke traffic must traverse inspection.

answers.text: Use ALB access logs as the primary source for VPC-internal east-west traffic analysis
Skip route summarization and advertise every /32 host route across the WAN
Route spoke traffic through the inspection VPC attachment
Place the customer gateway IP inside the VPC CIDR range

explanations.a: ALB logs only show traffic that reached the load balancer; VPC Flow Logs are the right tool for east-west analysis.
explanations.b: Per-host routes inflate the routing table and exceed BGP limits on Direct Connect (typically 100 prefixes).
explanations.c: Inspection is enforced only when the transit path steers packets through the appliance.
explanations.d: The customer gateway must be a public or routable IP outside the VPC CIDR; overlap breaks tunnel routing.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Production and development spokes must stay separated.

answers.text: Treat AWS PrivateLink as a layer 3 routed mesh between VPCs
Use DNS TTL values as a hybrid routing protocol
Use ACM-imported certificates without renewal monitoring or alerting
Place them in different Transit Gateway route tables or propagation domains

explanations.a: PrivateLink is a unidirectional service-endpoint model, not a routed IP mesh.
explanations.b: TTL controls how long a record is cached; it has no effect on packet routing decisions.
explanations.c: Imported certificates do not auto-renew; expiry causes outages without monitoring.
explanations.d: Separate route domains prevent unintended environment reachability.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A shared-services account owns the Transit Gateway.

answers.text: Share the Transit Gateway with application accounts through AWS RAM
Use AWS Firewall Manager only after each account opts in individually with no central policy
Create a public hosted zone to serve only VPC-internal DNS queries
Advertise the same prefix from every BGP peer with identical attributes

explanations.a: AWS RAM supports controlled cross-account sharing of supported network resources.
explanations.b: Firewall Manager is designed for centralized policy at the org/OU level; per-account opt-in defeats the purpose.
explanations.c: Public hosted zones are authoritative on the internet; private VPC-only resolution requires a private hosted zone.
explanations.d: Identical advertisements give the router no signal to choose between them; you need MED, AS_PATH, or LP differentiation.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A spoke subnet bypasses the intended appliance.

answers.text: Use an external CA without ACM Private CA for AWS-native certificate distribution
Correct the subnet route table to point required prefixes to the appliance path
Use VPC interface endpoints to expose your services to the public internet
Use AS_PATH prepending to make a path more preferred than its peer

explanations.a: AWS services integrate natively with ACM; an external CA without ACM PCA loses automated provisioning.
explanations.b: Subnet routes determine the next hop used by workload traffic.
explanations.c: Interface endpoints provide private connectivity into AWS; public exposure uses ALB/NLB or PrivateLink-as-provider.
explanations.d: Prepending lengthens AS_PATH and makes a path less preferred, not more preferred.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises clients need AWS private names.

answers.text: Choose subnets without ENA-supported instance types for high packet-per-second workloads
Use Global Accelerator to reduce data egress charges to on-premises
Deploy Resolver inbound endpoints and configure conditional forwarding on-premises
Use a single shared CDK app deployed manually for production and dev

explanations.a: High-PPS workloads require ENA-supported instance types; non-ENA instances cap throughput.
explanations.b: Global Accelerator improves anycast latency but does not reduce egress pricing to on-premises.
explanations.c: Inbound endpoints receive forwarded queries for private AWS namespaces.
explanations.d: Dev and prod should be separate stacks/accounts with isolated state and pipelines.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: AWS workloads need on-premises names.

answers.text: Skip BFD and rely on default BGP keepalive timers for sub-second failover
Use CloudFront access logs to monitor inter-VPC traffic between private subnets
Use the AWS CLI from a developer laptop as the production deployment automation tool
Deploy Resolver outbound endpoints and forwarding rules

explanations.a: Default BGP timers detect failure in tens of seconds; BFD is required for sub-second detection.
explanations.b: CloudFront logs cover edge requests; VPC-internal east-west traffic is captured by VPC Flow Logs.
explanations.c: Production deployments need a controlled pipeline (CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, etc.) with auditability and least privilege.
explanations.d: Outbound endpoints send selected VPC queries to corporate DNS.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Multiple accounts need the same DNS forwarding rule.

answers.text: Share Resolver rules and associate them with the required VPCs
Use 169.254.x.x link-local addresses for production application traffic
Disable AWS Config to reduce read-API throttling on networking resources
Use IP target groups for in-VPC EC2 targets that already have an instance ID

explanations.a: Shared rules keep hybrid DNS behavior consistent across accounts.
explanations.b: Link-local addresses are reserved for tunnel endpoints (e.g., VPN BGP) and not valid for production data flows.
explanations.c: Config is needed for compliance and drift; disabling it does not address API throttling.
explanations.d: Instance target groups are simpler and follow Auto Scaling lifecycle; IP targets are for non-EC2 or cross-VPC IPs.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A VPC still resolves public answers instead of corporate private answers.

answers.text: Skip CloudFormation drift detection and trust manual change tickets
Associate the forwarding rule with the VPC and confirm clients use the VPC resolver
Use an ALB host-based routing rule to load balance non-HTTP TCP services
Use a Site-to-Site VPN as the only path for sustained 10 Gbps throughput

explanations.a: Drift detection catches out-of-band changes that tickets often miss; it should run on a schedule.
explanations.b: The rule affects only associated VPCs whose clients query the expected resolver.
explanations.c: ALB is HTTP/HTTPS only; non-HTTP TCP requires a Network Load Balancer.
explanations.d: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels are limited to ~1.25 Gbps each and are not the right design for sustained 10 Gbps; Direct Connect is.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Overlapping DNS authority creates inconsistent answers.

answers.text: Use IAM roles in place of resource policies for cross-account access
Use a Direct Connect public VIF to reach a private VPC subnet
Define authoritative suffix ownership and conditional forwarding boundaries
Use Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints inside an isolated subnet without on-prem reachability

explanations.a: Cross-account access typically requires both: a trust policy on the role and a resource policy granting access.
explanations.b: Public VIFs reach AWS public service endpoints, not private VPC IP space; that requires a private or transit VIF.
explanations.c: Clear boundaries prevent ambiguous answers and resolver loops.
explanations.d: Outbound endpoints need network reachability to on-prem resolvers via DX/VPN; isolation defeats the integration.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises DNS should resolve interface endpoint private DNS.

answers.text: Use a single route table for all subnets in a multi-tier VPC
Use AWS PrivateLink to share full IP-level connectivity between two VPCs
Use NLB cross-zone load balancing without enabling it explicitly per target group
Forward to a VPC resolver path that has private DNS enabled for the endpoint

explanations.a: Public and private tiers need distinct route tables (e.g., IGW vs NAT) to enforce egress paths properly.
explanations.b: PrivateLink exposes specific service endpoints, not full IP-level reachability; use peering or TGW for that.
explanations.c: NLB cross-zone is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per target group.
explanations.d: Private endpoint names resolve correctly only inside the associated VPC resolver context.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An untrusted VPC sends traffic to production.

answers.text: Segment route tables and inspect traffic with AWS Network Firewall or appliances
Use Reachability Analyzer for live packet capture and DPI
Use a Route 53 alias record pointing to an on-premises IP
Use sticky sessions to compensate for missing identity tokens in API calls

explanations.a: Routing boundaries and inspection reduce exposure between trust zones.
explanations.b: Reachability Analyzer is a static configuration analyzer; it does not perform live packet capture.
explanations.c: Alias records target AWS resources by name; on-premises IPs require A/AAAA records or CNAMEs.
explanations.d: Stickiness binds a client to a target but does not authenticate or authorize requests.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A database should accept only application-tier traffic.

answers.text: Use BGP local preference on routes received from a remote AS to influence the remote AS choice
Reference the application security group in the database security group rule
Disable VPC Flow Logs and rely on application logs alone for network forensics
Change only an IAM password policy to fix a routing issue

explanations.a: Local preference is non-transitive and only affects outbound choice within the local AS; remote AS uses MED.
explanations.b: Security group references permit tier-specific access without broad CIDR exposure.
explanations.c: Application logs cannot reconstruct dropped packets, port scans, or layer 3/4 anomalies that flow logs capture.
explanations.d: IAM password policy governs human credentials; routing problems require route tables, BGP, or security group changes.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Private subnet egress must be inspected.

answers.text: Use Network ACLs as a stateful application-layer firewall
Manually document the setting in a spreadsheet only
Route default egress to centralized firewall or proxy endpoints
Use conditional forwarding rules instead of public hosted zones for internet-facing names

explanations.a: Network ACLs are stateless and operate at layers 3/4; they do not understand application protocols.
explanations.b: Documentation alone does not enforce configuration; the change must exist in the AWS resources themselves.
explanations.c: Traffic must be steered through the inspection point before reaching the internet.
explanations.d: Conditional forwarders route DNS queries to specific resolvers; they do not publish authoritative public records.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: S3 access through a VPC endpoint should be limited to one bucket.

answers.text: Use VPC peering to lower data transfer cost between two Regions
Use a NAT gateway as a stateful inspection firewall for east-west traffic
Use hardcoded VPC IDs and subnet IDs in CloudFormation templates promoted across environments
Scope the endpoint policy to the approved bucket and actions

explanations.a: Inter-Region peering still incurs cross-Region data transfer rates; the pricing is similar to other inter-Region paths.
explanations.b: NAT gateways translate addresses and do not inspect or filter east-west VPC traffic.
explanations.c: Hardcoded resource IDs prevent reuse across environments; pass them as parameters or use cross-stack references.
explanations.d: Endpoint policies constrain which resources can be accessed through the private endpoint.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Shared inspection must not be bypassed.

answers.text: Remove direct spoke-to-spoke routes that avoid the inspection attachment
Use longer subnet masks on AWS than on-premises so on-prem always wins routing decisions
Use a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint to forward queries from VPCs to on-prem resolvers
Disable BGP MD5 authentication on a Direct Connect peering session

explanations.a: Bypass routes defeat the intended security boundary.
explanations.b: Longest-prefix match means the more specific route wins; this guarantees AWS wins, not on-prem.
explanations.c: Inbound endpoints accept queries from on-prem; outbound endpoints forward VPC queries on-prem.
explanations.d: Disabling MD5 weakens the BGP session against spoofing and offers no operational benefit.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A stateless NACL blocks response traffic.

answers.text: Connect SD-WAN appliances directly to a Direct Connect gateway without a Transit Gateway
Allow the required ephemeral return ports in the NACL
Use CloudTrail to detect packet-level anomalies in VPC traffic
Use AWS Backup as a network configuration drift detection tool

explanations.a: SD-WAN integration uses Transit Gateway Connect (GRE+BGP); DXGW alone does not support SD-WAN attachments.
explanations.b: Network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic requires explicit allowance.
explanations.c: CloudTrail records control-plane API calls; packet-level analysis requires VPC Flow Logs or Traffic Mirroring.
explanations.d: AWS Backup is a data protection service and does not analyze network resource configuration.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: All VPC Flow Logs should be centralized.

answers.text: Use MX records to route HTTPS web traffic
Use a transit VIF to reach a VPC without a Transit Gateway attachment
Create flow logs for required scopes with delivery to a central CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination
Use single-AZ deployments to reduce inter-AZ data transfer fees and improve resiliency

explanations.a: MX records direct mail delivery; web traffic uses A/AAAA, alias, or CNAME records.
explanations.b: Transit VIFs terminate on a Direct Connect gateway connected to a Transit Gateway; without a TGW the VPC is unreachable.
explanations.c: Central delivery makes network metadata available for organization-wide analysis.
explanations.d: Single-AZ saves traffic costs but eliminates HA; resiliency requires multi-AZ.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Transit Gateway needs attachment-level traffic visibility.

answers.text: Use AWS WAF as a layer 4 firewall for non-HTTP TCP traffic
Use NAT gateway in every private subnet to maximize redundancy and minimize latency
Use a default route to the Internet Gateway in private subnets that need NAT
Enable Transit Gateway Flow Logs and monitor attachment metrics

explanations.a: WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS only; layer 4 protection comes from security groups, NACLs, or Network Firewall.
explanations.b: One NAT gateway per AZ is the recommended pattern; per-subnet NAT inflates cost without resilience benefit.
explanations.c: A default route to the IGW makes the subnet public; private subnets must point default to a NAT gateway.
explanations.d: Transit telemetry shows bytes, packets, and flow behavior by attachment.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Direct Connect utilization must alert at a threshold.

answers.text: Create CloudWatch alarms on Direct Connect throughput metrics
Use full-mesh VPN tunnels to scale to hundreds of VPCs
Use a Route 53 health check to register a domain name
Use IAM policies to enforce VPC-to-VPC routing restrictions

explanations.a: Direct Connect metrics can trigger capacity and health notifications.
explanations.b: Full-mesh VPN scales as O(n^2) and quickly hits operational limits; Transit Gateway is the scalable hub.
explanations.c: Domain registration is a separate Route 53 operation; health checks only monitor endpoints.
explanations.d: IAM controls API authorization, not packet routing; routing decisions live in route tables and TGW route tables.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Network Firewall must support investigations.

answers.text: Use a single Direct Connect connection without redundancy or VPN backup
Send alert and flow logs to a protected central destination
Configure jumbo frames on a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Use VPC sharing to share security groups across non-shared subnets

explanations.a: A single DX violates resilience guidance; AWS recommends two diverse circuits or a VPN backup.
explanations.b: Firewall logs identify rule matches and traffic decisions.
explanations.c: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames; MTU is fixed at 1500 with lower MSS after IPsec overhead.
explanations.d: Security group sharing follows shared subnets; non-shared subnets cannot reference cross-account security groups.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: DNS queries from workloads must be analyzed.

answers.text: Use AWS Config to capture per-packet flow data
Use the same BGP ASN on both sides of an eBGP session over Direct Connect
Enable Route 53 Resolver query logging
Use a security group as the authoritative DNS zone

explanations.a: Config tracks resource configuration changes, not network packet data.
explanations.b: eBGP requires different ASNs on each side; identical ASNs cause routes to be rejected as loops.
explanations.c: Resolver logs show the domain names queried from VPC resources.
explanations.d: Security groups filter packets at ENIs; they have no DNS authority or zone-serving capability.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: NAT gateway cost and saturation need dashboards.

answers.text: Use Transit Gateway Network Manager as a real-time intrusion detection engine
Use an ACM public certificate to sign internal mTLS traffic between EC2 instances
Use overlapping CIDRs across all VPCs and let routing protocols resolve conflicts
Use CloudWatch NAT gateway metrics with alarms and dashboards

explanations.a: Network Manager provides topology and event monitoring; intrusion detection belongs to GuardDuty or third-party IDS.
explanations.b: Public ACM certs are issued for public domains; internal mTLS uses ACM Private CA.
explanations.c: AWS networking does not arbitrate overlapping CIDRs; address conflicts must be designed out before connecting VPCs.
explanations.d: NAT metrics expose bytes, packets, drops, and error indicators.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: VPC workloads must resolve corp.example.com on-premises.

answers.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint and forwarding rule for corp.example.com
Connect EC2 instances directly to a Direct Connect dedicated port without a VIF
Send VPC Flow Logs only to local instance memory for short-term review
Use TLS passthrough on an ALB to inspect HTTPS payloads

explanations.a: The forwarding rule sends matching VPC queries to corporate DNS.
explanations.b: Traffic on Direct Connect must traverse a VIF (private/public/transit); EC2 instances cannot peer with the port directly.
explanations.c: Flow logs must be delivered to S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Firehose; instance memory is not a supported destination.
explanations.d: ALB always terminates TLS at the listener; passthrough is a Network Load Balancer behavior.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises DNS must resolve aws.internal in Route 53.

answers.text: Use VPC peering to provide transitive routing through a hub VPC
Create an inbound Resolver endpoint and an on-premises conditional forwarder
Use a single Lambda function in place of an Application Load Balancer for path-based routing
Use service-linked roles as a substitute for security groups

explanations.a: VPC peering is non-transitive; a hub VPC cannot relay traffic between two peered spokes.
explanations.b: The inbound endpoint gives on-premises DNS a private target for AWS-hosted names.
explanations.c: A Lambda function as the front door does not provide listeners, sticky sessions, or load balancing semantics.
explanations.d: Service-linked roles grant API permissions to AWS services; they do not gate network traffic.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Overlapping private zones give unexpected answers.

answers.text: Configure DNSSEC by adding a TXT record only, without DS or KSK setup
Use static routes only on a BGP-capable Direct Connect for change management
Correct zone associations and suffix authority for the affected VPCs
Use Transit Gateway Connect over IPsec instead of GRE

explanations.a: DNSSEC requires a Key Signing Key in Route 53 and a DS record published at the parent zone; a TXT record alone does nothing.
explanations.b: Direct Connect requires BGP for the peering session; static-only configuration is not supported on the AWS side.
explanations.c: Private hosted zone answers depend on VPC association and resolver path.
explanations.d: Transit Gateway Connect uses GRE encapsulation with BGP; IPsec is not the supported transport for Connect attachments.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A central Resolver rule is not used by a spoke VPC.

answers.text: Use AWS RAM to share an Internet Gateway across multiple accounts
Treat VPC Traffic Mirroring as a real-time alarm engine without a monitoring appliance
Use Transit Gateway to connect VPCs that share identical primary CIDR blocks without translation
Associate the shared Resolver rule with the spoke VPC

explanations.a: Internet Gateways are not shareable resources in AWS RAM; each VPC has its own IGW.
explanations.b: Traffic Mirroring duplicates packets to a target appliance; alerts come from the appliance, not the mirror itself.
explanations.c: Transit Gateway requires non-overlapping CIDRs between attached VPCs unless NAT or PrivateLink mediates traffic.
explanations.d: Shared rules are effective only after VPC association.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: DNS queries loop between AWS and on-premises.

answers.text: Remove circular forwarding and define a single authoritative resolver for each suffix
Use an ALB listener rule for routing between networks
Use a Classic Load Balancer for new HTTP/2 and gRPC workloads
Use AWS Trusted Advisor as a packet-capture utility

explanations.a: Forwarding loops create repeated referrals until queries time out.
explanations.b: ALB listener rules route HTTP requests to target groups; they do not route between VPCs or hybrid networks.
explanations.c: Classic Load Balancer does not support HTTP/2 or gRPC; ALB is required.
explanations.d: Trusted Advisor is a best-practice checker, not a packet-capture tool.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Two Regions need the same private namespace.

answers.text: Skip IaC and rely on point-in-time AWS Console screenshots for repeatability
Associate the private hosted zone with every required VPC or implement an approved shared DNS model
Use a centralized egress VPC without route tables that point to the inspection appliance
Use AWS Cloud Map as a layer 4 transparent proxy
