explanations.a: Screenshots cannot be replayed and do not capture dependencies; IaC is the supported path.
explanations.b: Private zone visibility must be extended to each VPC that needs the namespace.
explanations.c: Centralized egress requires explicit route table entries pointing to the firewall/proxy in the inspection VPC.
explanations.d: Cloud Map is a service registry returning DNS or API answers; it does not proxy traffic.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Users should reach the lowest-latency healthy endpoint.

answers.text: Use a single hosted zone for both internet and split-horizon private records without separation
Use VPC peering to extend multicast across VPCs without Transit Gateway multicast support
Configure Route 53 latency routing with health checks
Use only CloudFront cache settings to control private VPC routing

explanations.a: Split-horizon DNS requires distinct public and private hosted zones for the same domain.
explanations.b: VPC peering does not propagate multicast; Transit Gateway multicast domains are required.
explanations.c: Latency routing can return a healthy endpoint that is close to the requester.
explanations.d: CloudFront cache controls edge caching, not VPC routing or hybrid traffic flow.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A canary release needs 10% DNS traffic.

answers.text: Use service control policies in place of route table entries
Use a private hosted zone associated with one VPC to resolve names from a peered VPC without re-association
Use a NAT gateway as the application load balancer
Configure weighted routing records

explanations.a: SCPs restrict API actions across accounts and have no effect on dataplane routing.
explanations.b: Private hosted zones must be associated with each VPC that needs to resolve their records, even across peering.
explanations.c: NAT gateways translate addresses for outbound traffic and have no listener, target group, or layer 7 capability.
explanations.d: Weighted records support controlled traffic distribution across endpoints.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A standby endpoint should be used only after primary failure.

answers.text: Configure failover routing with health checks
Disable VPC route propagation and manage every prefix manually at scale
Skip TLS in transit because IPsec already encrypts at layer 3
Use IGMP snooping at the security group level

explanations.a: Failover routing returns secondary answers when the primary health check fails.
explanations.b: Manual route management does not scale; propagation from VGW/TGW is required for hybrid networks.
explanations.c: IPsec encryption ends at the tunnel termination; defense in depth still recommends TLS for application traffic.
explanations.d: Security groups operate per ENI and do not implement IGMP snooping; that is a switch-fabric feature.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Users in specific countries must use regional endpoints.

answers.text: Use DNS TTL values as a hybrid routing protocol
Configure geolocation routing records
Use ACM-imported certificates without renewal monitoring or alerting
Place the customer gateway IP inside the VPC CIDR range

explanations.a: TTL controls how long a record is cached; it has no effect on packet routing decisions.
explanations.b: Geolocation routing chooses answers from configured location rules.
explanations.c: Imported certificates do not auto-renew; expiry causes outages without monitoring.
explanations.d: The customer gateway must be a public or routable IP outside the VPC CIDR; overlap breaks tunnel routing.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A complex policy combines weights and failover.

answers.text: Create a public hosted zone to serve only VPC-internal DNS queries
Advertise the same prefix from every BGP peer with identical attributes
Use Route 53 traffic flow or traffic policies
Use AWS Firewall Manager only after each account opts in individually with no central policy

explanations.a: Public hosted zones are authoritative on the internet; private VPC-only resolution requires a private hosted zone.
explanations.b: Identical advertisements give the router no signal to choose between them; you need MED, AS_PATH, or LP differentiation.
explanations.c: Traffic policies help model reusable multi-rule DNS decisions.
explanations.d: Firewall Manager is designed for centralized policy at the org/OU level; per-account opt-in defeats the purpose.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An HTTPS health check fails because the service expects a host name.

answers.text: Use ALB access logs as the primary source for VPC-internal east-west traffic analysis
Treat AWS PrivateLink as a layer 3 routed mesh between VPCs
Skip route summarization and advertise every /32 host route across the WAN
Configure the health check protocol, host name, path, and expected response

explanations.a: ALB logs only show traffic that reached the load balancer; VPC Flow Logs are the right tool for east-west analysis.
explanations.b: PrivateLink is a unidirectional service-endpoint model, not a routed IP mesh.
explanations.c: Per-host routes inflate the routing table and exceed BGP limits on Direct Connect (typically 100 prefixes).
explanations.d: Health checks must test the same endpoint behavior that represents real availability.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: AWS workloads need on-premises hostnames.

answers.text: Configure outbound Resolver endpoints, forwarding rules, security groups, and routes
Use VPC interface endpoints to expose your services to the public internet
Use Global Accelerator to reduce data egress charges to on-premises
Use an external CA without ACM Private CA for AWS-native certificate distribution

explanations.a: Hybrid name resolution needs DNS forwarding plus network access to corporate resolvers.
explanations.b: Interface endpoints provide private connectivity into AWS; public exposure uses ALB/NLB or PrivateLink-as-provider.
explanations.c: Global Accelerator improves anycast latency but does not reduce egress pricing to on-premises.
explanations.d: AWS services integrate natively with ACM; an external CA without ACM PCA loses automated provisioning.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: On-premises users need AWS private hosted zone names.

answers.text: Skip BFD and rely on default BGP keepalive timers for sub-second failover
Deploy inbound Resolver endpoints in associated VPCs
Use a single shared CDK app deployed manually for production and dev
Use CloudFront access logs to monitor inter-VPC traffic between private subnets

explanations.a: Default BGP timers detect failure in tens of seconds; BFD is required for sub-second detection.
explanations.b: Inbound endpoints let external DNS forward AWS private namespace queries to Route 53 Resolver.
explanations.c: Dev and prod should be separate stacks/accounts with isolated state and pipelines.
explanations.d: CloudFront logs cover edge requests; VPC-internal east-west traffic is captured by VPC Flow Logs.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Resolver endpoints need high availability.

answers.text: Disable AWS Config to reduce read-API throttling on networking resources
Use the AWS CLI from a developer laptop as the production deployment automation tool
Place endpoint IPs in subnets across multiple Availability Zones
Choose subnets without ENA-supported instance types for high packet-per-second workloads

explanations.a: Config is needed for compliance and drift; disabling it does not address API throttling.
explanations.b: Production deployments need a controlled pipeline (CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, etc.) with auditability and least privilege.
explanations.c: Multiple endpoint IPs reduce the impact of an AZ or subnet failure.
explanations.d: High-PPS workloads require ENA-supported instance types; non-ENA instances cap throughput.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A firewall blocks hybrid DNS.

answers.text: Use 169.254.x.x link-local addresses for production application traffic
Skip CloudFormation drift detection and trust manual change tickets
Use IP target groups for in-VPC EC2 targets that already have an instance ID
Allow TCP and UDP 53 between resolvers and endpoint IPs

explanations.a: Link-local addresses are reserved for tunnel endpoints (e.g., VPN BGP) and not valid for production data flows.
explanations.b: Drift detection catches out-of-band changes that tickets often miss; it should run on a schedule.
explanations.c: Instance target groups are simpler and follow Auto Scaling lifecycle; IP targets are for non-EC2 or cross-VPC IPs.
explanations.d: DNS can use UDP and TCP, so both protocols must be permitted.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: All domains are forwarded both ways.

answers.text: Replace catch-all forwarding with suffix-specific rules and ownership boundaries
Use IAM roles in place of resource policies for cross-account access
Use Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints inside an isolated subnet without on-prem reachability
Use an ALB host-based routing rule to load balance non-HTTP TCP services

explanations.a: Specific rules prevent recursive loops and accidental authority conflicts.
explanations.b: Cross-account access typically requires both: a trust policy on the role and a resource policy granting access.
explanations.c: Outbound endpoints need network reachability to on-prem resolvers via DX/VPN; isolation defeats the integration.
explanations.d: ALB is HTTP/HTTPS only; non-HTTP TCP requires a Network Load Balancer.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Private DNS for an interface endpoint fails from another VPC.

answers.text: Use AWS PrivateLink to share full IP-level connectivity between two VPCs
Check endpoint DNS scope, VPC associations, and forwarding paths
Use a single route table for all subnets in a multi-tier VPC
Use a Site-to-Site VPN as the only path for sustained 10 Gbps throughput

explanations.a: PrivateLink exposes specific service endpoints, not full IP-level reachability; use peering or TGW for that.
explanations.b: Endpoint private DNS is scoped and must be reachable through the correct resolver path.
explanations.c: Public and private tiers need distinct route tables (e.g., IGW vs NAT) to enforce egress paths properly.
explanations.d: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels are limited to ~1.25 Gbps each and are not the right design for sustained 10 Gbps; Direct Connect is.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: The zone apex must point to CloudFront.

answers.text: Use sticky sessions to compensate for missing identity tokens in API calls
Use a Direct Connect public VIF to reach a private VPC subnet
Create an alias A or AAAA record
Use NLB cross-zone load balancing without enabling it explicitly per target group

explanations.a: Stickiness binds a client to a target but does not authenticate or authorize requests.
explanations.b: Public VIFs reach AWS public service endpoints, not private VPC IP space; that requires a private or transit VIF.
explanations.c: Alias records support apex names for supported AWS targets.
explanations.d: NLB cross-zone is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per target group.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A SaaS provider asks for domain verification.

answers.text: Use BGP local preference on routes received from a remote AS to influence the remote AS choice
Change only an IAM password policy to fix a routing issue
Use AS_PATH prepending to make a path more preferred than its peer
Create the provider-specified TXT record

explanations.a: Local preference is non-transitive and only affects outbound choice within the local AS; remote AS uses MED.
explanations.b: IAM password policy governs human credentials; routing problems require route tables, BGP, or security group changes.
explanations.c: Prepending lengthens AS_PATH and makes a path less preferred, not more preferred.
explanations.d: TXT records commonly hold domain verification values.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: An IPv6 endpoint needs DNS.

answers.text: Create an AAAA or alias AAAA record
Use conditional forwarding rules instead of public hosted zones for internet-facing names
Manually document the setting in a spreadsheet only
Use Reachability Analyzer for live packet capture and DPI

explanations.a: AAAA records return IPv6 addresses.
explanations.b: Conditional forwarders route DNS queries to specific resolvers; they do not publish authoritative public records.
explanations.c: Documentation alone does not enforce configuration; the change must exist in the AWS resources themselves.
explanations.d: Reachability Analyzer is a static configuration analyzer; it does not perform live packet capture.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Reverse DNS is required for an address.

answers.text: Disable VPC Flow Logs and rely on application logs alone for network forensics
Create a PTR record in the correct reverse zone
Use VPC peering to lower data transfer cost between two Regions
Use a NAT gateway as a stateful inspection firewall for east-west traffic

explanations.a: Application logs cannot reconstruct dropped packets, port scans, or layer 3/4 anomalies that flow logs capture.
explanations.b: PTR records map IP addresses back to hostnames.
explanations.c: Inter-Region peering still incurs cross-Region data transfer rates; the pricing is similar to other inter-Region paths.
explanations.d: NAT gateways translate addresses and do not inspect or filter east-west VPC traffic.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A non-apex subdomain should point to a vendor DNS name.

answers.text: Use a Route 53 alias record pointing to an on-premises IP
Use longer subnet masks on AWS than on-premises so on-prem always wins routing decisions
Create a CNAME record
Disable BGP MD5 authentication on a Direct Connect peering session

explanations.a: Alias records target AWS resources by name; on-premises IPs require A/AAAA records or CNAMEs.
explanations.b: Longest-prefix match means the more specific route wins; this guarantees AWS wins, not on-prem.
explanations.c: CNAME records map one non-apex name to another canonical name.
explanations.d: Disabling MD5 weakens the BGP session against spoofing and offers no operational benefit.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A child zone is delegated to another team.

answers.text: Use Network ACLs as a stateful application-layer firewall
Use a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint to forward queries from VPCs to on-prem resolvers
Use AWS Backup as a network configuration drift detection tool
Create NS records for the child zone in the parent zone

explanations.a: Network ACLs are stateless and operate at layers 3/4; they do not understand application protocols.
explanations.b: Inbound endpoints accept queries from on-prem; outbound endpoints forward VPC queries on-prem.
explanations.c: AWS Backup is a data protection service and does not analyze network resource configuration.
explanations.d: NS records delegate authority for a subdomain.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: DNSSEC signing is enabled in Route 53. What completes the chain of trust?

answers.text: Publish the DS record at the registrar or parent zone
Use MX records to route HTTPS web traffic
Connect SD-WAN appliances directly to a Direct Connect gateway without a Transit Gateway
Use a transit VIF to reach a VPC without a Transit Gateway attachment

explanations.a: The parent DS record lets validating resolvers verify the child zone's signing keys.
explanations.b: MX records direct mail delivery; web traffic uses A/AAAA, alias, or CNAME records.
explanations.c: SD-WAN integration uses Transit Gateway Connect (GRE+BGP); DXGW alone does not support SD-WAN attachments.
explanations.d: Transit VIFs terminate on a Direct Connect gateway connected to a Transit Gateway; without a TGW the VPC is unreachable.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Which key is created for Route 53 DNSSEC signing?

answers.text: Use hardcoded VPC IDs and subnet IDs in CloudFormation templates promoted across environments
A key-signing key associated with a customer managed KMS key
Use single-AZ deployments to reduce inter-AZ data transfer fees and improve resiliency
Use AWS WAF as a layer 4 firewall for non-HTTP TCP traffic

explanations.a: Hardcoded resource IDs prevent reuse across environments; pass them as parameters or use cross-stack references.
explanations.b: Route 53 uses a key-signing key backed by KMS for DNSSEC signing.
explanations.c: Single-AZ saves traffic costs but eliminates HA; resiliency requires multi-AZ.
explanations.d: WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS only; layer 4 protection comes from security groups, NACLs, or Network Firewall.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Resolvers report DNSSEC validation failure.

answers.text: Use IAM policies to enforce VPC-to-VPC routing restrictions
Use a Route 53 health check to register a domain name
Verify DS values, KSK status, hosted zone signing, and registrar publication
Use a default route to the Internet Gateway in private subnets that need NAT

explanations.a: IAM controls API authorization, not packet routing; routing decisions live in route tables and TGW route tables.
explanations.b: Domain registration is a separate Route 53 operation; health checks only monitor endpoints.
explanations.c: A mismatch in the chain of trust breaks validation.
explanations.d: A default route to the IGW makes the subnet public; private subnets must point default to a NAT gateway.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A DNSSEC key rollover is planned.

answers.text: Use a single Direct Connect connection without redundancy or VPN backup
Use NAT gateway in every private subnet to maximize redundancy and minimize latency
Use full-mesh VPN tunnels to scale to hundreds of VPCs
Maintain parent and child key alignment throughout the rollover

explanations.a: A single DX violates resilience guidance; AWS recommends two diverse circuits or a VPN backup.
explanations.b: One NAT gateway per AZ is the recommended pattern; per-subnet NAT inflates cost without resilience benefit.
explanations.c: Full-mesh VPN scales as O(n^2) and quickly hits operational limits; Transit Gateway is the scalable hub.
explanations.d: The zone can fail validation if DS records and signatures are out of sync.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A third-party registrar hosts the domain registration.

answers.text: Confirm the registrar supports publishing DS records
Use a security group as the authoritative DNS zone
Configure jumbo frames on a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Use AWS Config to capture per-packet flow data

explanations.a: The registrar must publish DS records for the delegated domain to maintain DNSSEC validation.
explanations.b: Security groups filter packets at ENIs; they have no DNS authority or zone-serving capability.
explanations.c: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames; MTU is fixed at 1500 with lower MSS after IPsec overhead.
explanations.d: Config tracks resource configuration changes, not network packet data.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: The team asks what DNSSEC protects.

answers.text: Use VPC sharing to share security groups across non-shared subnets
It protects DNS response integrity through cryptographic validation
Use an ACM public certificate to sign internal mTLS traffic between EC2 instances
Use the same BGP ASN on both sides of an eBGP session over Direct Connect

explanations.a: Security group sharing follows shared subnets; non-shared subnets cannot reference cross-account security groups.
explanations.b: DNSSEC helps resolvers detect tampered DNS responses.
explanations.c: Public ACM certs are issued for public domains; internal mTLS uses ACM Private CA.
explanations.d: eBGP requires different ASNs on each side; identical ASNs cause routes to be rejected as loops.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: All VPCs should use central DNS forwarding rules.

answers.text: Use CloudTrail to detect packet-level anomalies in VPC traffic
Connect EC2 instances directly to a Direct Connect dedicated port without a VIF
Share Resolver rules from a central DNS account and associate them with VPCs
Send VPC Flow Logs only to local instance memory for short-term review

explanations.a: CloudTrail records control-plane API calls; packet-level analysis requires VPC Flow Logs or Traffic Mirroring.
explanations.b: Traffic on Direct Connect must traverse a VIF (private/public/transit); EC2 instances cannot peer with the port directly.
explanations.c: Shared rules keep forwarding behavior consistent across accounts.
explanations.d: Flow logs must be delivered to S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Firehose; instance memory is not a supported destination.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: A business unit owns its namespace but uses central corporate forwarding.

answers.text: Use VPC peering to provide transitive routing through a hub VPC
Use service-linked roles as a substitute for security groups
Use a single Lambda function in place of an Application Load Balancer for path-based routing
Use distributed private zones with shared central Resolver forwarding

explanations.a: VPC peering is non-transitive; a hub VPC cannot relay traffic between two peered spokes.
explanations.b: Service-linked roles grant API permissions to AWS services; they do not gate network traffic.
explanations.c: A Lambda function as the front door does not provide listeners, sticky sessions, or load balancing semantics.
explanations.d: This model preserves local namespace ownership while reusing central resolver paths.

questions.name: Network Implementation
questions.text: Spoke VPCs reach central Resolver endpoints over Transit Gateway.

answers.text: Allow DNS routes and security group rules to the endpoint IPs
Use Transit Gateway Network Manager as a real-time intrusion detection engine
Configure DNSSEC by adding a TXT record only, without DS or KSK setup
Use static routes only on a BGP-capable Direct Connect for change management

explanations.a: Central DNS requires packet reachability to the endpoint addresses.

questions.name: Network Implementation

questions.name: Network Implementation

Use VPC peering to extend multicast across VPCs without Transit Gateway multicast support
Use Transit Gateway Connect over IPsec instead of GRE

Disable VPC route propagation and manage every prefix manually at scale

questions.name: Network Implementation

Use a Site-to-Site VPN as the only path for sustained 10 Gbps throughput

Use a Route 53 alias record pointing to an on-premises IP

Use longer subnet masks on AWS than on-premises so on-prem always wins routing decisions

explanations.d: Longest-prefix match means the more specific route wins; this guarantees AWS wins, not on-prem.

Record the event, changed resources, actions, results, and rollback status
Use a NAT gateway as a stateful inspection firewall for east-west traffic
Use BGP local preference on routes received from a remote AS to influence the remote AS choice

Connect SD-WAN appliances directly to a Direct Connect gateway without a Transit Gateway

questions.name: Network Implementation

Use hardcoded VPC IDs and subnet IDs in CloudFormation templates promoted across environments
Supply public IPs, ASNs, and tunnel preferences through controlled inventory or parameters

Use a pipeline step or custom resource to keep vendor controller state and AWS resources aligned

Use CloudTrail to detect packet-level anomalies in VPC traffic
